items.name: No pay tier for high, middle, and low performers; the review as never a managing-out file; pay as never a lever; and what reaches Session 14 in what form
items.desc:
**Routed to: S14 (`86ajgmjk1`)**

Session 13 separated review from pay by design and fixed the point system's inputs as the seat's horizon, the markers, and the days, on records and never on any judgment of a person; a person who holds a seat's horizon and never unlocks earns the horizon's weight and the pool's growth and is not "partially meets." Session 14 inherits: no performance tier may add a pay line, a marker, a weight, or a withheld anything, because her "pay for performance" is carried by the unlock, the markers, the pool's weighting, and the days, and a low performer's pay does not move; no review record may be cited in a managing-out decision or in any performance conversation, as no evidence line, scorecard, reset record, or coaching record may (S9 P42; S12 P7), because a review holds only the person's words and the stack's states; whatever Session 14 designs for a person whose work is not holding is not a review and does not wear its form (the block, the record, the one question); her "compensation conversations can be a helpful tool" when managing someone out (Book p.418) is refused whole, because pay is not a lever anyone holds; and the review's dimension 3 reads the fact of a non-negotiable line and never discusses one, so the destination after the flag (`86akht39y`) is not the review. The review's states (the horizon held, the range's counts, the supplied items) are readable by Session 14's mechanism only as the person can read them, and the "something new" mark is a candor line on the lead's entry and never evidence about the person. This extends `17tn048qcjt`, `86akht39y`, `86akhpvqx`, `86akh67yy`, and `17tn048qc2e` and does not repeat them. High.

items.name: A lead's review, the domain's upward halves read by mechanism, the Maitre d's review load and own pay page, a departure's final pay, and managing out against a pay system with no lever
items.desc:
**Routed to: S15 (`86ajgmjpw`)**

Session 13 built every floor review as the Maitre d's and left a lead's own review with no holder until `86akhb2jg` closes, with the team's reading that the holder is whoever holds the lead's check-in, on the same form, against the lead's own sheet (dimension 1 as holding a domain without an apex, dimension 2 from the lead's own advocate record, dimension 3 as the lead's range on the leads' review record, dimension 4 as what the building supplied to the lead's seat including its languages), and that the lead's upward half is the domain's read of the lead, aggregated from the domain's reviews' upward halves by mechanism and never by person. Session 15 inherits: the design of a lead's review as managing managers, including whether the two leads' reviews of their domains are calibrated against each other at the leads' review (the team's reading is no, because there is nothing to calibrate, and that the "something new" counts per lead are the only cross-lead read); the Maitre d's review load (reviews held, moved, and extended) beside the coaching load as the reset's first read, with the refused carriers standing; the Maitre d's own pay page, points, and salaried rule as a seat's and never a person's; a departure's final pay, which under the architecture is the days worked and the accrued share to the last pay date, with what counsel requires on final pay and any pool share for the last day as counsel's; and managing out against a pay system that has no raise to withhold, no bonus to deny, and no rating to lower, so that Session 15's mechanism cannot use pay and must say so. This extends `17tn048qcjx`, `86akhcz7f`, `86akht3bw`, `86akh5uy1`, `86akh680c`, `86akhpvtf`, and `17tn048qc2g` and does not repeat them. High.

items.name: The founders' own pay and review, the partners' place in the pool, the founders as the first explainers of item 6, and the founders as the leads' default review holders
items.desc:
**Routed to: S16 (`86ajgmjz6`)**

Session 13 recorded nothing about Brandon's or Dominic's pay, review, or working style, and marked every place the architecture touches them as Session 16's. Session 16 inherits four things. Whether the partners hold points in the pool at all: the record distributes the pool "to the whole team" and the founders are not the team, so the team's reading is that the partners are outside the pool and paid under the operating agreement, which is founder-gated with `86akh3x9m` and `86akh3t62`; under branch A the chef partner is a founder and the same question applies to the chef seat, under branch B the chef seat is a salaried seat in the pool. The founders' own review: the record's "feedback runs both directions" reaches the center nowhere (`86akh2qzy`), and Session 4's domain read is the only mechanism by which a founder is read; whether the founders' domains are reviewed on the four dimensions in any form is Session 16's. The founders complete the compensation mechanics and review module's lead half pre-opening before the first interview they run (A17), beside their interviewer training and Session 12's coaching module, which is a founder load on the founders' seats and not interiority; and the founders are the first explainers of item 6 to the two leads, so the mechanics page must exist as a mechanism with unset values before the leads' first interviews (A12). And until `86akhb2jg` closes the founders hold the first leads' reviews by default as they hold their check-ins (`17tn048qcjz`), reading a lead against the lead's own sheet and writing nothing in a founder's voice, which is the one review a founder holds and is bound by every rule on the S13 page. This extends `17tn048qcjz`, `86akht3e4`, `86akhb2xe`, `86akhpvub`, `86akh5uy9`, `86akh2qzy`, and `17tn048qc2h` and does not repeat them. Normal.

items.name: Rows 155 to 168, the review page and the mechanics page beside the destinations and feedback pages, eleven instrument extensions, thirteen findings routed, "review" and "points" as vocabulary lines, and the no-pay-input rule beside the other structural rules
items.desc:
**Routed to: S17 (`86ajgmk27`)**

The readiness test stands at one hundred and sixty-eight rows; rows 160, 161, 163, 166, and 168 carry a founder-gated hold inside them and are read as failed until it closes, and rows 157, 162, and 165 are read at the first reset as well as the gate. Session 17's assembly inherits: the review page (A13) and the mechanics page (A12) as the wiki's review and pay pages beside the destinations page (`86akht1m9`), the feedback culture page (`17tn048qck5`), and the communication architecture page (S11 I1), with the parameters register on the partners' page and never on the wiki; eleven instrument specifications that extend earlier sessions' (I1 extends S4's person page and S9's career conversation block; I2 extends S4's placement and S12's placed check-in trigger; I3 extends S12's coaching form; I4 extends S4's person page and S5's transparency sheet; I5 extends S3's registers and S5's item 6; I6 extends S5's seat sheet; I7 extends S4's loop-closure window and S11's channel; I8 sits under S7's module standard beside S12's coaching module; I10 extends S11's reach read record; I11 extends S5's transparency sheet) and must be assembled as one instrument each; two vocabulary lines as audit rules beside the "operating system," "diagnostic," and "feedback" lines (`86akh5uym`; S11 P27; S12 finding 18.3): "the review," unqualified, is the person's review and every other review is named in full, and "points," unqualified, is the pay system's word and appears on no other surface, so that no recognition, designation, or channel item is ever described with it; the rule that no review output and no feedback act reaches pay and the point system reads four inputs on records (A26, A27) beside Session 6's four dimensions, Session 9's order of every read, Session 10's no-person-in-a-room rule, Session 11's record-first rule, and Session 12's no-page rule; the transparency sheet's item 6 as a mechanism with values set or unset, assembled from I5 and never from anywhere else; and thirteen findings, four of which surface from a narrow read of the white paper's review paragraph and pay section and nine of which need the record against the transparency line, the service model, the daypart thesis, the stack's open decisions, and both canon artifacts, for the assembly's conflicts list, including the finding that "exploitation" is undefined in both canon artifacts as "toxicity" is (S12 18.9), for the same ruling. This extends `17tn048qck2`, `17tn048qc2j`, `86akht3fx`, `86akhpvvq`, and `86akhcz7t` and does not repeat them. High.

comments.text: Session 13 built the review rubric as the four scorecard dimensions Session 6 fixed, read at review as states from records the person can already read and never as marks on any scale: competency for the seat as the horizon held on the seat sheet's field 6 and the next unlock's date; self-directed mastery as the invisible advocate's own record listed with dates; conduct under the non-negotiables and inside the range as the range-used count's states and the fact of a non-negotiable line or none; and what the building supplies as supplied, not supplied, or not yet per item the person named, scored on the building. The hiring bar and the review bar are the same seat sheet read at two points, and nothing is added at review that was not read at hiring. On the second collision, her compensation machinery does not transfer as form and two of its three principles transfer as function (legible, defensible), while the third, connected to a review, is refused by design: no review output reaches pay, and what carries pay for performance is the unlock, the fluency markers, the pool's daily weighting, and the days. The figure and the data source this item's description names were not used; the record's own statement that the percentage is still being finalized is the one Session 13 follows, and financials are not a context source for this program. S13 page, sections 3, 9, and 12; P6, P7, P22, P23, P36, P37.

Session 13 read the gap this item names as two documents rather than one, following Session 2's split. The commitments are the charter's people section, confirmed by the founders (`86akh3t9p`), and they are the philosophy stated as commitments (labor as an asset, pay for what matters, dignity, built into price and never a service charge, the whole team including the kitchen, no hierarchy of importance, fluency recognized, benefits from the start). What Session 13 adds is the written account of the mechanism a person can explain in their own words, the compensation mechanics page (work item A12): the two layers, one pool per day, the four inputs and the refused inputs, what a day is, the daily calculation in words, the payment rhythm, the markers, the salaried rule, the routed pay lines, and where a question goes, in every house language, the single source the transparency sheet's item 6 reads from. Every person completes a module on it on shift, and every lead and founder completes it before handing item 6, so that the strongest operational commitment the house has made is one its own team can articulate. No percentage appears anywhere in the chain. S13 page, sections 9, 13, and 14; P22 to P26, P38, P39, P41.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 closed the pay half Session 8 left open. Sŏn has no levels and no pay bands, and pay progression is carried without a rung by the seat sheet's weights at each of field 6's horizons, moved on the date the domain lead records a readiness form the assessor scored, so that the record's "direct line between learning and earning" is a mechanism and no lead's judgment is in it. The functions a ladder carries in pay (a visible pay path, recognition of growth, a legible day-one answer) are carried by the published weights on the sheet and the transparency sheet's item 6, the fluency markers, and the pay page, which shows every weight move with its form and date. A lead enters at the lead seat's entry horizon, priced as the seat's salary and weight with no rank in the name. Note 72's ladder that describes outcomes rather than skills is refused with the ladder; the readiness rows already read acts in a service at a horizon that reads judgment. S13 page, sections 10 and 12; P28, P29, P37.

Session 13 built the architecture against the commitments as Session 2 listed them and Session 5 stated them on item 3, with the four elements this item names designed as mechanisms and no figure anywhere: the percentage is a row on a parameters register with the founders and Dominic's domain as owner and the financial model as its basis; the point weights are seat properties at each horizon on the seat sheet, moved by recorded unlocks, with the values on the same register; the daily calculation is the person's points over the day's total points times the day's pool, one pool per calendar day for the whole house, written to the person's pay page by the next morning; the payment rhythm is the same pay date as base pay and never slower, bounded by counsel and the platform; and the cross-strand premium is a marker on while current inside Session 8's window, with cross-period fluency recognized the same way. Dominic's review of the commitment list (`86akh3t9p`) stands as the condition the architecture sits under, and the rows an offer needs are placed ahead of the leads' offers. S13 page, section 9; P22 to P26, P29.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 priced cross-strand fluency as a marker: an on-or-off addition to the person's points on every day it is on, on while Session 8's two readiness forms and the seat held on each strand are current inside the window and off when the window lapses, never graded, never a dimension, a rank, or a seat, with its value a founder-gated row on the parameters register set with Dominic's domain against the record's "recognized in compensation as meaningful." Cross-period fluency is recognized on the same mechanism, because a day counts once and a person who holds two periods on one day would otherwise earn nothing for the second register. The alternative for cross-period fluency, recognition in connections and the succession pool's order only, is stated and not recommended. S13 page, section 10.3; P29, P26.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 closed the review half: the review measures against the four scorecard dimensions read as states from records, and the principles enter the review only as Session 12 placed them in coaching, as behaviors inside dimension three (conduct under the non-negotiables and inside the range) and never as a fifth thing or a rating scale. Her peer-review prompt that asks which operating principle a person most embodies is refused, because a principle is never a rating scale and a peer's account of a peer is a refused source. Principles version one, when it exists, is marked per principle as a feedback reference, a commitment, or an operating rule (S12 P35), and a review reads a feedback-reference principle exactly as coaching does, from an act on a record. S13 page, sections 3.3 and 6.2; P7, P14.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 built "no surprises" as a mechanism in three halves. The stack assembles the review from the records the person can already read, the person's own captures from the close among them, and the lead adds nothing. A lead holding something not on a record says nothing of it at the review and asks the stack to place a check-in, where it is said as a hypothesis. The review ends with a read-back and one question, whether anything said was not on the page; the answer is a mark on the review record, and a review marked "something new" is a candor line on the lead's entry at the leads' review and a count on the mechanism, never a read of the person and never a reason to shorten the interval. Every review item carries the date of the line or state it cites, and an item with no citation cannot be entered. S13 page, section 4; P9, P10; readiness rows 157 and 158.

Session 13 fixed that no lagging indicator drives the point system beyond the pool's own base: a person's points never rise or fall with food cost, labor percentage, or a period's revenue, and the four inputs are the seat's weight at the horizon held, the markers, the days, and the salaried rule. The pool's base is a founder-gated parameter with one constraint recommended: it must not shrink when the generosity range is used, so a comped item counts at menu price and recovery spend does not reduce the day's pool, because a base that punishes the range makes the team pay for its own generosity. The generosity range's value and the financial recovery threshold are set by Dominic's domain against the financial model, written on the holder's range card in the seat's languages, versioned, reaching the holder by the check-in and the sheet's version before the brief, and read at the reset against the range-used and escalation counts; the values are founder-gated and appear nowhere in this program. S13 page, sections 9.2, 9.4, and 11.6; P22, P23, P35.

Session 13 picked the review's rhythm inside the record's range: six months, on the person's own clock, the first review six months after the first paid hour and each six months after the last, placed by the stack with no review season, as a reset parameter with the record's three-month floor, shortened only if reviews change a path line or a supplied line the check-ins had not touched. The review opens on the person page whole since the last review and reads ten records the person can already read and nothing else. The payment rhythm: the pool share is paid with base pay on the same pay date and never on a slower cycle, with the cycle's length bounded by pay-date law (counsel's) and the payroll platform (to confirm), and the Realist's read that a rhythm slower than the market's makes the record's "reasonable" false at the first pay date; it is a founder-gated row on the parameters register and a duration, not a figure. S13 page, sections 2, 3, and 9.7; P3, P6, P24.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 decided that pay recognizes cross-period fluency, on the same mechanism as cross-strand fluency: a marker on while the period-plan readiness form and the seat held in each period are current inside the window, never a dimension or a rank, its value a founder-gated row on the register. The reason is the day's definition the architecture fixes: a day is a calendar day counted once, so a person who holds the morning window and dinner on one day works one day, and without a marker the second register the record's whole thesis depends on would earn nothing. One pool per calendar day for the whole house, rather than a pool per period, is the companion decision. The alternative, recognition in connections and the succession pool's order only, is stated and not recommended. S13 page, sections 9.2, 9.5, and 10.3; P22, P24, P29.

Session 13 designed the architecture as a mechanism with every value on a parameters register, which changes what "being finalized" can mean at a first interview: item 6 can be handed as the whole mechanism (the two layers, one pool per day, the four inputs, the day, the daily calculation, the rhythm, the markers, the pay page, where a question goes) with its values marked unset, which is more than the record's word and less than an offer needs; the team recommends a first interview may run in that state and no offer goes before the values, extending Session 5's P35 and leaving the ruling with the founders (`86akh7qry`). The rows an offer needs (the percentage, the base, the two lead seats' weights and salaries, the rhythm) are placed ahead of the leads' offers (`86akh9tb0`). The salaried line: Session 8's structural test stands and the founders ratify the list (`86akh9tbw`); Session 13 prices the class as a salary plus points in the pool on every open day by rule, with the outside-the-pool alternative stated, so the seats that get the dinner in the room are the seats on the ratified list. S13 page, sections 10.1 and 13.5; P28, P31, P39, P40.

Session 13 scored the review against the four dimensions in Session 6's terms and added nothing: competency for the seat as the horizon held on field 6 and the next unlock's date, written by the stack, with no "does not meet" because a person who did not hold a horizon would be a plan not held or a readiness read that reads not yet, neither of which is a review; self-directed mastery from the invisible advocate's record and never a lead's impression; conduct as the range-used count's states and the fact of a non-negotiable line or none; what the building supplies as supplied, not supplied, or not yet per item, scored on the building. Cross-strand and cross-period fluency are priced as markers and never scored. Finding 18.1 is closed as a mechanism: "cultural alignment" at hiring is dimension three at review, "growth potential" is dimension two, "the path forward" is the track re-read and never scored; it stays open as a sentence until the founders ratify the four dimensions as one list read at two points, which this item carries. S13 page, section 3; P6, P7, P8.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 fixed the review's relation to the sign-off: none. The review reads the progression state the stack wrote from the form the assessor scored and the lead recorded, and signs nothing, schedules nothing, hastens or delays nothing, and nominates no one, because a review that judged competency would judge an unlock, which Session 8's three-seat rule forbids any lead to do. The record's two conversations on page 19, the review and the competency conversation, are two mechanisms: the sign-off is the check-in at which the form is read (S8 P37) and the review is the six-month reading of the page whole. In pay, an unlock on the person's own seat moves the weight on the date the lead records the form, never waiting on a lead's judgment, and a cross-domain competency moves nothing until the seat is held, which is Session 13's reading of "a direct line between learning and earning" for the founders to ratify with the wording (`86akhcz22`). S13 page, sections 3.2, 7, and 10.4; P7, P17, P29, P31.

Session 13 gave the word its place. A salaried seat, on Session 8's structural test and the founders' ratified list, holds a salary as base pay and points in the pool on every day the house is open in the pay period, by rule and not by shift, because a seat that owns a domain across every open period has worked every day the domain ran; its weight is a seat property like any other, its upside on a full night is real, and a lead in the pool holds no conflict because a lead moves no one's points and holds no discretion over the pool. The alternative, salary alone outside the pool, is stated and not recommended; the founders decide with Dominic's domain. Base pay itself, which the record never describes and everywhere assumes, is the first layer of a two-layer architecture, and every wage-and-hour question the two layers raise is counsel's. S13 page, sections 9.1, 9.8, and 10.1; P22, P28, P31; finding 19.1.

comments.status: Answered by this page for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 named what a lead enters at in the architecture without altitude: the lead seat's entry horizon, priced as the seat's salary at that horizon and the seat's point weight, both seat properties on the lead's sheet and the same for whoever holds the seat. A lead's own unlocks (the other lead's domain read through the leads' review, the periods held as they open, cross-domain fluency like anyone's) add markers and connections as they add anyone's, and nothing else moves a lead's pay; "further along" for a lead is the same measure and the same mechanism as for a runner. There is no seat above a lead's to enter and no rank to name. The founders ratify with Session 8's two-webs reading (`86akh9tbz`). S13 page, section 10.2; P28, P31.

comments.status: Read by this page; extended for its S13 half.
comments.text: Session 13 read the five extensions for any that touch review or pay and found two that do. P39's reading that S5 I21's refusal of a hand-written training record applies only once the stack can write one is inherited by the review, which reads the training record's state and never a hand-written one; and P54's reference note for lead, domain-owner, and Branch B chef seats sits in the hiring packet and never reaches a review or a pay page, because hiring assessments never become a person's record. Nothing on the S13 page assumes any of the five were ratified, and Session 17 carries the packet whole. S13 page, sections 3.1 and 7; P6, P17.

Session 13 priced all four under Session 7's constraints and no figure. Mentoring is paid as shift and recognized as a teaching marker on the mentor's points on every day a plan they mentor is open, from the mentee's first paid hour to the plan's close, never per the mentee's outcome, and never stacked because a mentor holds one open plan. Authorship is a flat payment per module approved against the standard and again per versioned revision approved, paid with base pay, never a point, and never per completion by others. Completion: the record's "the more modules completed, the more earned" is read as carried by shift pay for every module hour and by the unlock's weight move, with no separate amount per module, because a per-module amount pays for completing rather than holding and is the volume incentive the standard exists to refuse; the alternative is stated and the reading is founder-gated. Training pay is base pay for every scheduled hour plus the seat's entry-horizon weight in the pool from the first paid hour, with no training weight below entry, because a reduced weight is a probation label written in pay. The readiness form travels to no review: the review reads only the progression state the stack wrote from it, never a row or a not-yet, and this is written as readiness row 158. S13 page, sections 3.1 and 11; P6, P32, P33, P34.

Session 13 took all four hand-offs. Both fluency markers are priced as markers on while current inside Session 8's window, never a dimension or rank, with cross-period fluency recognized because one day counts once. The salaried test is priced as a salary plus pool points on every open day by rule, with the alternative stated and the founders ratifying the list. A lead enters at the lead seat's entry horizon, priced as the seat's salary and weight with no rank. The review's relation to the three-seat advancement structure is none: the review reads the recorded state, signs nothing, and nominates no one; a weight moves on the date the lead records the form, and a cross-domain competency moves nothing until the seat is held, which is the team's reading of the learning-to-earning line for the founders to ratify with the wording. The threshold's value and the known limits are set by Dominic's domain on the range card, versioned, reaching the holder before the brief. S13 page, sections 7, 10, and 11.6; P17, P28, P29, P31, P35.

Session 13 built the review to open on the person page whole and find the career conversation block there: the path line and the one track in the person's words, re-read and re-written by the person in their own half of the review, with no pay line, no level, and no seat promise, because the review inherits every refusal of the career conversation. No diagnostic record is an input to the review, and the review reads no evidence line, scorecard section, or reset record, which is written as readiness row 158; the four dimensions stay four, and the list of records the review reads is closed by construction. The threshold's value and the known limits are set by Dominic's domain against the financial model, written on the holder's range card, versioned, and read at the reset, with the setting method on the page and the values nowhere in the program. S13 page, sections 3, 7, and 11.6; P6, P7, P17, P35.

Session 13 priced nothing by a designation: a designation carries no pay line, no marker, and no day, the rotation floor carries its load as development, and a load that the reset finds is a seat's is answered by a seat and never by a pay line on a designation; the tension the Realist sees, that holding the room is real load at the holder's own weight, is named and the rule held. The range's money values are set by Dominic's domain and written on the holder's range card in value in the seat's languages, so that the loose edge closes: a server told to use their judgment with no number is unprotected, and a value the holder cannot read is not a range. No environment behavior (a slot item spoken, participation in any mechanism, a designation's count, a recognition given or received) is a fifth dimension or an input to the review or to the point system, written as readiness rows 158 and 159. Mentoring recognition beyond shift is answered as the teaching marker. S13 page, sections 3.3, 9.4, 10.5, and 11; P7, P23, P30, P32, P35.

Session 13 priced translation on the authorship model as a flat payment per page version approved by the page's owner and a second holder of the language, paid with base pay, never a point, and again per version, with software-drafted translations paid on the holder's approval work; interpreting is a designation on the clock with no pay line beyond shift. No recognition, channel item, half-page, or communication behavior of any kind is a review input or a pay input, written as readiness rows 158 and 159. The pay parity read is designed as the reach read's tags applied to the three rates pay is a function of (the unlock rate, the marker rate, and the days scheduled per seat class), at the reset, with no name, figure, target, inference, or act on a person, reading "cannot read yet" until the tags and a year exist, with counsel bounding the data and the founders ruling the tags; it is founder-gated. The pulse's carrier: the review does not read the pulse composite, because the pulse is anonymous and the review is a person's, so nothing on the S13 page needs the carrier confirmed; it stays the Operations Lead's to confirm as Session 11 left it. S13 page, sections 3.1, 11.5, and 13.4; P6, P32, P39, P40.

Session 13 built the review to open on the person page's lines and on nine other records the person can already read, and on nothing else; it cites no coaching record, no failure-type count, no placed, extended, or moved check-in count, no recognition decline, no half-page "routed" mark, and no re-training trigger beyond the training record's state, written as readiness row 158. A review that contains something not on the page is a candor failure read on the lead's entry at the leads' review, written as readiness row 157: the review ends with a read-back and one question, whether anything said was not on the page, and the answer is a mark on the record; a lead holding something not on a record says nothing of it at the review and asks the stack to place a check-in. "You really have talent" as part of a formal process is the review's reading of the record aloud: the connections, the unlocks, the authored modules, the captures where a failure was absorbed unseen, and the range used well, read as specific acts on specific services in canon's register, with the lead reading what the person did and never saying what the person is. No feedback act of any kind is a pay input, a fifth dimension, or an input to the point system, and the point system's four inputs are on records and never on anyone's judgment, written as readiness row 159 and as the one thing on the S13 page a later session cannot revise at ordinary cost. S13 page, sections 3, 4, 5, and 12; P6, P9, P10, P13, P23, P36.

Session 13 priced the class Session 8 defined, for the founders to ratify with the list: a salaried seat holds a salary as base pay and points in the pool on every day the house is open in the pay period, by rule and not by shift, with its weight a seat property; the alternative, salary alone outside the pool, is stated and not recommended, because it would make a full night worth nothing to the two seats that hold it. The salary values are rows on the parameters register with the founders, Dominic's domain, and counsel as owners, and no value appears in the program.
